newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi predicts many countries in EMU first wave.
newsitem.headline: Prodi predicts many countries in EMU first wave.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that many countries would take part in the first wave of European Monetary Union (EMU).
"Everyone knows that there will be many countries in the first group because there is no alternative," he told Finnish television. A transcript of the interview was released by his office.
"The first group will be vast and it is necessary to be part of it because there is a law of clubs that says that the first to join are afterwards extremely severe with the others," he said.
He said Finland would "certainly" be part of the first group because it had made great strides in the past few years.
He repeated that he believed that Italy would be part of the first group to join because it was working hard to achieve entry criteria. "I believe that we will make it," he said.

Speaking at the foreign press club earlier on Tuesday, Prodi reaffirmed Italy's intention to be among founder members of the new euro from 1999 and proposed moving the deadline for parliamentary passage of the country's 1998 budget forward by four months to mid-August to boost confidence.
A key criterion for EMU membership will be whether a country's 1997 public deficit is within three percent of its gross domestic product.

Many economists doubt whether Italy can meet the three percent ratio this year despite a tough 62.5 trillion lire ($38 billion) budget. Prodi himself has said a mini-budget is probable following a deficit overshoot in 1996.
